author: Hotochin
text:
Hey Guys,

Harry----This is something that you wrote in an above post. -"but you
dont need to learn everything to be able to trade, if you master one
setup you can pretty much use that all the time. some master traders
here in RTM have loved one setup and use that all the time."

What is hard for me with this statement is how to know what a "set up"
is. The Marketpedia section is wonderful at explaining many different
things, but there is really no point at which to start. Its hard to know
 what to look for where. There are QM,engulf's, FO, CP, and diamonds all
 over the place. And once you narrow those down, do I always need a FL?
How about a QM? You see what I mean? Its like if I took a car apart for
you and you knew nothing about cars. You are looking at parts all in
front of you. Then I told you to start with the transmission. Now I just
 gave you the answer as to how to start. The problem is that you don't
know what a transmission is anyways. So even though you have an answer,
it really does not help. I tried my best to explain my issue here,
hopefully you understand what I am saying. Any thoughts?

H

author: Aaron
text:
Scott,

I hope you don't mind me giving my view on this buddy. What I think
Harry means when he says that, is, take for instance a textbook engulf
setup, price is heading to supply, price on the LTFs engulf an important
 low indicating bearish intention and then take the RT to a cap or FTR,
this is a set up I love seeing and I am seeing it more and more.

The QM could be a setup on its own as long as you are using the HTF S/D zones etc...

One could just look for a fake out in a HTF area etc...

I think the thing to do, and which has helped me a lot is study one
setup and study it till u know it inside out, the you will understand
what Harry means mate.

I have tried to explain how I think, but as you know no trader is the same, so take this with an open mind my friend.

DT

Hotochin, my friend!

I hear a lot of frustration in your voice. The frustration is
understandable, I have been through a LOT of FX frustration even after
joining RTM! However, the frustration is not necessary. If we look to
other sucessful traders here, we can be sure that it can be done!

Concerning what you have written: I got your point! But imagine it as a
menu in such a kind of restaurant where you can set up your menu on your
 own from available ingredients. You can decide what side dish, what
kind of meat, etc etc etc. Here it is the same. You have individual
components and it is up to you what dish you will create.

So, let's choose one setup! In the following picture you can see my PL curve from Forex Tester 1. Looks good, doesn't it?

I concentrated only on one setup:

1: I identified H4 FTR's and price caps (all of them).

2: I waited for price to engulf a level and return to one below
above.(here, the main difference between FT1 and real time trading
shows: in FT1 you can fast forward PA so you don't have to wait days...
and it is also the main reason I cannot reach such success in real life:
 I AM IMPATIENT!!!! )

3: So once PA got into a H4 level, I switched to M15 and waited for a QM or break and retest of M15 S/R line.

4: TP - opposite H4 level, SL - some 15 - 20 pips below/above pivot

Of course, the PL curve shown above is UNREALISTIC for me in real life
due to my lack of patience.... but I am working on it! Also, well, I
knew there would be a big drop in 2008 in advance... so I could act
accordingly and concentrate on shorts mainly!

So my dear Hotochin, if you find the setup interesting, try to find some
 examples and you can put them here in my journal or in yours... Let's
work on it together mate!

LP

hello Scott,

what i meant to say there is that Markepedia is full of powerful
concepts that you need to explore and take one step further as DT1 said.

what i meant about the "Masters loving one setup", take Kruger for
example, i bet he has studied all the material but his trademark is the
QM and CP.

then Pedini loved the engulf of the FL and patiently waited for the
return, and many other not Masters but Associates (still) have picked
their style. some with more rounded up style than others, but this
proves my statement that you can be successful even if you master one
setup only. and i dont mean you dont need to study the rest. study as
much as you can and master as many as you can, but in the end everyone
will have their favorite, thats all i mean.

you are right that Markepedia has so many things to look at at first.
well.. you see most of the older guys came from other places and had
been around when these concepts first started to be discussed about. we
did realize however (a bit late) that newer guys may need a bit of
guidance where to start so thats why include a small list of startup
articles now in the welcome/signup letter of new members similar to the
one in that post LP mentioned above.

author: Aaron
text:
Hi Scott,

I have made some remarks on your chart, IMO you're right about the FTRs.

From the left where the SR gets engulfed, price essentialy failed to
return to this demand creating the first FTR in black, notice from the
black FTR we had an engulf of the high, I have not marked it on the
chart, but should be easy enough to see, we then had a FTB to the FTR,
this FTB was yet another attempt to return to demand, however failed to
make the LL, so the FTB is another FTR , where we did get a reaction.
Once we had a reaction, you marked another FTR (SUPPLY - white) which
needed for me to be engulfed, and it was, once this was engulfed look at
 how easy the entry would have been at DP that created the engulf to get
 long, The reward to risk was fantastic.

DT
